title: Caprese Salad
subtitle: fresh mozzarella, ripe tomato, and basil
excerpt: Caprese is the simplest of Italian summer dishes. Ripe tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, and basil with a drizzle of good olive oil. Nothing is cooked. The quality of the ingredients is everything.
sourceNotes: Insalata caprese comes from the island of Capri off the coast of Naples. The red, white, and green of the dish mirror the colours of the Italian flag.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Slice tomatoes and mozzarella up to 30 minutes ahead. Add basil and oil just before serving.

content.text: This dish has no recipe to speak of -- only technique and ingredients. Use the ripest tomatoes available and the freshest mozzarella you can find. The olive oil should be good enough to taste on its own.

items.prepNote: use 125g fresh mozzarella per person, sliced

content.text: Slice the tomatoes and mozzarella to the same thickness, about 1cm.
Lay the tomato and mozzarella slices on a platter. Alternate them and let them overlap slightly.
Scatter fresh basil leaves across the top.
Drizzle generously with olive oil. Season with flaked salt and black pepper. Serve immediately.

items.fix: Use only ripe tomatoes and never store them in the fridge.

items.cause: Not fresh buffalo mozzarella or served too cold
items.fix: Bring mozzarella to room temperature for 20 minutes before slicing.

content.text: Caprese comes from the island of Capri and the broader Campania region of southern Italy. The red, white, and green of the dish mirror the Italian flag. It is eaten all over Italy in summer and appears on almost every Italian restaurant menu worldwide. Outside Italy, it is often over-dressed -- the original is notable for its restraint.
